title: Pöschl-Teller type of Jaynes-Cummings Hamiltonians: SUSY transformations
authors: İsmail Burak Ateş, Şengül Kuru, Javier Negro, Efe Serbest
abstract: The aim of this work is to define and investigate the generalized Jaynes-Cummings (JC) Hamiltonian by means of supersymmetric (SUSY) quantum mechanics methods. We have considered trigonometric and hyperbolic Pöschl-Teller (PT) potentials as two natural ingredients to modify the standard JC model. We show that these generalized JC Hamiltonians have a list of characteristics in common with the JC Hamiltonian, for example: matrix intertwining, excitation number symmetry, Rabi frequency, formulas for atomic inversion and classical and revival times. Therefore, we conclude that JC Hamiltonians can be considered as one example of a wider a class of generalized Hamiltonians which can be useful in broader interaction problems.
summary: This paper generalizes the Jaynes-Cummings model by incorporating Pöschl-Teller potentials within the framework of Supersymmetric Quantum Mechanics. The authors establish a hierarchy of partner Hamiltonians and demonstrate that these generalized models retain key physical symmetries of the original JC model. This suggests that the JC interaction belongs to a wider, mathematically tractable class of interacting quantum systems.
main_problem: To define and investigate generalized Jaynes-Cummings (JC) Hamiltonians using supersymmetric (SUSY) quantum mechanics methods.
main_result: The generalized JC Hamiltonians, built using Pöschl-Teller potentials, share key characteristics with the standard JC model, suggesting they belong to a broader class of solvable interacting systems.
method: The study employs SUSY quantum mechanics, utilizing shape-invariant hierarchies and intertwining relations to construct and analyze partner Hamiltonians.
model_or_system: The system models the interaction between an atom and a quantized field, generalized by replacing standard photon operators with those derived from trigonometric or hyperbolic Pöschl-Teller (PT) potentials.
key_observables: Atomic inversion ($\langle\sigma_3angle$), Rabi frequency ($\Omega$), classical and revival times ($T_{cl}, T_{rev}$), and energy eigenvalues ($\epsilon_{n,\pm}^\ell$).
important_parameters: Detuning parameter ($\delta$), coupling coefficient ($ eta$), and the order index ($\ell$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a shape-invariant hierarchy $\{H_\ell\}$ factorizable by first-order operators, and the structure relies on specific ansatz forms for intertwining operators.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of atomic inversion for coherent states under different partner Hamiltonians ($k=0, 1, 4$) and compare spectra for scalar and matrix Hamiltonians.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the generalized JC Hamiltonian using SUSY methods, then establishing a hierarchy of partner Hamiltonians via intertwining relations, and finally analyzing the time evolution and spectral properties for both trigonometric and hyperbolic PT potentials.
why_interesting: This work provides a systematic, mathematically rigorous framework (SUSY) to generalize fundamental models in quantum optics (JC model) using exactly solvable potentials (PT), yielding insights into anharmonic dynamics and spectral symmetries.
